subject.title: lossless-claw bootstraps into quarantine after every Gateway restart due to new sessionId generating fresh JSONL file

question: Should OpenClaw accept `session.restartContinuation` as the opt-in contract for preserving aborted main-session ids across controlled Gateway restarts, or should this wait for a broader restart-recovery design?
rationale: The source-level gap is real enough to keep tracking, but the proposed solution adds a new compatibility-sensitive session config surface and changes session-state reuse semantics.

options.title: Sponsor the linked opt-in
options.body: Review and land the linked PR if maintainers accept an explicit `session.restartContinuation` knob for this narrow Gateway restart continuity case.

options.title: Require a config-free design
options.body: Keep this issue open but redirect the fix toward generic restart recovery that does not add a session config knob.

options.title: Decline this direction
options.body: Close this issue and the linked PR if maintainers decide OpenClaw should not preserve aborted session ids across restarts for this workflow.

recommendation.title: Sponsor the linked opt-in
recommendation.body: Review and land the linked PR if maintainers accept an explicit `session.restartContinuation` knob for this narrow Gateway restart continuity case.

likelyOwner.reason: They merged the terminal-main transcript reconciliation behavior that the proposed fix modifies and have adjacent session transcript history in the same path.
